name: Cristina Fernández de Kirchner
summary: Peronist president who governed with an interventionist state: nationalisations, price controls, exchange controls and expanded social transfers, alongside same-sex marriage and gender identity laws. Abroad she criticised market fundamentalism and the IMF and sought reform of global financial rules.

ban-spanking.rationale: Ley 26.994 art. 647 prohibits corporal punishment of children in any form.

capital-controls.rationale: Her government imposed foreign-exchange restrictions in 2011 to curb capital flight.

collective-bargaining.rationale: She boasted of the twelfth year of free collective bargaining (paritarias) setting wages.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: At the UN in 2009 she held developed countries responsible for emissions and called for binding common rules.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: She demanded that Security Council and General Assembly resolutions be respected by all members, including permanent members such as the UK on the Malvinas.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Ley 26.741 art. 1 makes hydrocarbon self-sufficiency and exploration a national priority.

expand-nuclear.rationale: She listed Atucha II and a fourth nuclear plant among government achievements and highlighted nuclear plants built in 2014.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Ley 26.737 limits foreign ownership of rural land to 15% instead of banning it, so foreigners may own land.

free-public-college.rationale: Ley 27.204 declares undergraduate study at state institutions free and bans fees or charges.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Ley 26.743 lets people change legal gender by self-declaration, with no judicial or medical requirement.

human-caused-global-warming.rationale: In 2009 she said developed nations are responsible for emissions.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: She stressed Argentina's leading position on non-proliferation and nuclear energy for peaceful purposes only (2013, 2015 UN speeches).

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Ley 26.425 eliminated the private capitalisation regime and absorbed it into the public pay-as-you-go SIPA.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: In 2012-2014 UN speeches she affirmed Israel's right to live securely within its borders alongside a Palestinian state.

limit-campaign-donations.rationale: Ley 26.571 set campaign-spending limits and free media space.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: In her 2008 UN speech she said the market does not allocate resources to the most vulnerable and the state must link society and market; in 2009 she attacked "market fundamentalism".

military-force-for-human-rights.rationale: In 2013 she said her country opposed direct intervention and bombing in Syria, arguing it would cause more deaths and that peace and security are political, not military, concepts.

multipolar-world.rationale: In 2011 she called for a more pluralistic and diverse world and a more democratic UN, abolishing the permanent-member category and the veto.

national-resource-control.rationale: Ley 26.741 expropriated 51% of YPF to recover control of hydrocarbons; she also stated resource sovereignty at the UN.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Ley 26.994 art. 437 lets either spouse petition for divorce alone, with no fault to prove.

one-spouse-at-a-time.rationale: Ley 26.994 art. 403 makes an existing marriage a bar to marrying again.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Ley 26.991 lets the executive set maximum prices and penalises hoarding and abusive price rises.

price-controls-fight-inflation.rationale: Ley 26.991 strengthened maximum-price powers and penalties as the supply law during high inflation.

price-stability-first.rationale: Ley 26.739 widened the Central Bank mission to include employment and development with social equity beside currency stability.

prohibit-child-medical-transition.rationale: Ley 26.743 art. 11 gives minors access to treatments through legal representatives and a minor's consent, so the law she enacted does not prohibit them.

public-ownership.rationale: Her government took YPF stake, Aerolíneas Argentinas and the private pension funds into public hands; the record covers several major industries.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: She said nobody from the IMF would tell Argentina what to do after it paid the Fund off, and called for lending without conditionality.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: She called for reform of the multilateral financial institutions and common rules for developed and developing countries.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Her government enacted and she promulgated Ley 26.618 opening civil marriage to same-sex couples.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: At the UN she described the fight against impunity for the dictatorship's crimes as state policy.

shut-down-tax-havens.rationale: She called for eliminating tax havens at the G20.

vote-at-sixteen.rationale: Ley 26.774 gives all Argentines of 16 political rights including the vote.

notes: Record-based answers come from laws she promulgated.
